verdict.rationale: Isaac ROS packages are built on ROS 2 and are described as deployable across workstations and Jetson embedded systems, implying some abstraction across compute/hardware targets, and Isaac Sim can ingest sensors/robots from multiple formats (URDF, CAD, USD) — suggesting hardware-agnostic configuration. However, no evidence explicitly documents a stable HAL layer for swapping physical sensors/actuators without application rewrites, nor examples of doing so. Missing for 10: explicit hardware-abstraction-layer documentation, sensor/actuator driver interchangeability examples, and hands-on evidence of swapping hardware without code changes.
